The [abbreviation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/CliffordAlgebra/Spin/LowRank/Six/SpecialLinear.lean#L1036) identifies the actual native Spin group of three hyperbolic planes with `SL₄(K)`, by its even half-spin action. I checked [`splitEvenForm`](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Spin/Polarization/Split/Even.lean#L52): it is the evaluation form on `(K³)* × K³`, hence the split six-dimensional form, not an arbitrary rational or real form. The field has `2 ≠ 0`; algebraic closure is unnecessary for this split specialization. The chosen polarization and basis specify the isomorphism, so noncomputable basis choices do not claim a canonical identification independent of that data.

The key [Layer6 convention](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/SpinRepresentations/README.md#L840) is respected: even Clifford units of reverse norm one give `GL₄`, whereas Spin also requires vector preservation. The [determinant-one membership theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/CliffordAlgebra/Spin/LowRank/Six/SpecialLinear.lean#L1020) proves both inclusions, and [the application formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/CliffordAlgebra/Spin/LowRank/Six/SpecialLinear.lean#L1055) verifies that the displayed equivalence is the restriction of the same half-spin `GL₄` map. Its bijectivity proof at932 checks faithfulness through the two-block Clifford model and surjectivity through explicit elementary-transvection lifts; [`toMatrix_spinPlusAction_spinSixTransvectionLift`](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/CliffordAlgebra/Spin/LowRank/Six/SpecialLinear.lean#L828) supplies their actual matrices. Thus the result does not identify Spin with the larger norm-one group.

No separate tagged acceptance example is listed for this split equivalence; the required full-membership and faithful-surjective milestones above are proved without `sorry` in the inspected source. Other dimensions, arbitrary-form transport, and the vector/exterior-square representation comparison are further Layer6 statements. No successful local compilation or independent consultation of Fulton–Harris/Book of Involutions is claimed.

The [global monodromy statement](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/Complex/Conformal/GlobalBranch.lean#L214) agrees in the scalar case with [Honda's complex-analysis notes, Corollary31.3](https://www.math.ucla.edu/~honda/math520/notes.pdf), and realizes [human roadmap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/ConformalMapping/README.md#L118) L4. The source validly extends the conclusion to complete complex normed targets using analytic germs and the identity theorem; no finite-dimensional target assumption is smuggled in.

ContinuesInside quantifies every continuous path from z₀ staying in U and requires an actual locally compatible analytic continuation along each one. It does not assume a global function. Membership z₀∈U rules out vacuity, and openness upgrades equality near z₀ within U to the ordinary neighborhood germ appearing in the conclusion. Simple connectivity supplies paths and homotopies; neither a globally holomorphic initial representative nor analyticity outside U is asserted.

Chosen paths and terminal germs define F pointwise, but the source proves its local agreement with every continued germ before deducing analyticity. Thus arbitrary choices cannot alter the branch on U. The [converse construction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/Complex/Conformal/Continuation/Basic.lean#L535) shows that holomorphic functions genuinely satisfy the continuation premise. L4 prescribes no separate tagged Check for this theorem; logarithm/root applications and reflection are additional targets. The primary scalar reference does not itself establish the Banach-valued extension, which was assessed from the source.

The [homotopy monodromy theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/Complex/Conformal/Monodromy.lean#L386) has the same fixed-endpoint conclusion as [Honda, Theorem31.2](https://www.math.ucla.edu/~honda/math520/notes.pdf). Here continuability is required along every slice of the specified homotopy, which is the exact local hypothesis needed instead of continuability along all paths of a surrounding domain. This matches [human roadmap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/ConformalMapping/README.md#L118) L4.

IsAnalyticContinuationAlong requires analyticity at each moving point and local equality of germs at neighboring parameter values; it is not an arbitrary assignment of unrelated analytic functions. The same initial germ is explicitly imposed for all slices. No continuity in the homotopy parameter of the chosen representatives is assumed: local uniqueness of continuation supplies the needed compatibility. The conclusion is germ equality at the common endpoint, not global equality of representatives. Complete complex normed targets are supported by the source's analytic identity theorem; the cited reference covers the scalar specialization.

The [null-homotopic-loop consequence](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/Complex/Conformal/Monodromy.lean#L430) passes and returns the initial germ. The anonymous example beginning at line450 supplies continuations from a holomorphic function on an open neighborhood of the homotopy, so the hypotheses are satisfiable. L4 lists no separately tagged Check for this theorem. A loop around a singularity cannot be contracted through that singularity while retaining the continuation hypotheses.

The [basis](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Hermite/Function/HilbertBasis.lean#L101) is the Hermite-function basis of L² of **Lebesgue measure on ℝ**, as its displayed signature and docstring say. The naming announcement's Gaussian-measure wording describes the separate measure-side basis. Here the probabilists' polynomials Heₙ(√2x) are multiplied by exp(−x²/2)/√(n!√π). This normalization agrees, after the √2 change of variable, with the two Hermite rows in [DLMF18.3.1](https://dlmf.nist.gov/18.3#T1).

The [human roadmap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/Completed/OrthogonalL2Bases/README.md#L185) A3 explicitly distinguishes these two carriers and requires an element-level export. That requirement passes in [coe_hermiteHilbertBasis](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Hermite/Function/HilbertBasis.lean#L118): the constructed basis is the actual Hermite family, not an arbitrary separability witness. Positive normalization constants exclude division/square-root junk, and the exponential-moment argument supplies completeness rather than assuming density as an unproved hypothesis.

All A3 acceptance checks have source witnesses in [Parseval.lean](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Hermite/Function/Parseval.lean#L52): polarized Parseval (line52), the norm-square sum (line59), and coordinates of every basis vector (line75), hence ψ₀ has coordinate lp.single 2 0 1, the ℓ² version of the prescribed finite-support vector. Taking f=g=ψ₀ gives the explicit Parseval example, with its unit norm proved in [Orthonormal.lean](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Hermite/Function/Orthonormal.lean#L123). These general RCLike proofs specialize to both ℝ and ℂ; this is a source-level specialization, not a newly compiled example. Ladder, oscillator and Fourier eigenfunction assertions are separate targets.

The [inequality](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/Complex/Conformal/SchwarzPick/Derivative.lean#L103) matches the exact formula in [Oprea, Math220B Lecture17, p.2](https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~doprea/220w26/lec17.pdf), and supplies the infinitesimal [human roadmap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/ConformalMapping/README.md#L107) Schwarz–Pick target. Both z and f(z) lie strictly inside the unit disc, so both denominators are positive. DifferentiableOn on this open set supplies the genuine derivative at z, avoiding the zero derivative assigned to a nondifferentiable function.

There is no assumption f(0)=0; the source's Möbius conjugation supplies that normalization internally. At z=0 the estimate becomes |f′(0)|≤1−|f(0)|², and when f(0)=0 it is Schwarz's derivative bound. Constants have zero left side, while the identity map has equality. No unproved equality-rigidity assertion is bundled into this inequality. Multiplying the Poincaré metric by a constant does not alter this contraction estimate, so there is no missing factor two.

L2 lists no separately tagged Check for this derivative bound. The [bundled-disc companion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/Complex/Conformal/SchwarzPick/Derivative.lean#L138) uses the same inequality on Complex.UnitDisc, confirming the strict-disc carrier. Disc-automorphism classification and the global hyperbolic distance estimate are separate results.

The [abstract zero-one law](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Probability/Exchangeability/PathSpace/HewittSavage.lean#L175) is correctly restricted to exchangeable events. The rendered short signature hides a crucial instance: in the pinned source hs is MeasurableSet[exchangeableSigma α] s, not arbitrary product measurability. That σ-algebra requires invariance under finitely supported coordinate permutations. Without this restriction an ordinary one-coordinate event could have any probability.

The assumptions separately require invariance of the path law and independence of cylinders on disjoint finite coordinate blocks. Exchangeability alone would not imply zero-one: a nontrivial mixture of constant sequences is a counterexample. The apparently weaker finite-measure hypothesis is safe: choosing both blocks empty and both cylinder sets universal in hprod forces ρ(univ)=ρ(univ)², so a finite such law is zero or normalized. The zero law satisfies the conclusion, and for a probability law this is the usual Hewitt–Savage setting. No standard-Borel hypothesis is needed for the cylinder approximation argument.

Commutativity, finite projectivity of B/A and finite presentation of C/B are explicit; faithful flatness, positive constant rank and reducedness are not needed.

I inspected the construction rather than treating any equivalence as the universal property. A finite projective module is represented using a split finite free module, with coordinate functionals. The inverse constructs the quotient-algebra map from the coordinates of an actual point, and both inverse identities are proved at [lines 181–195](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/RingTheory/WeilRestriction.lean#L181). The bare definition does not require E elliptic or D invertible, and does not promise an elliptic curve for those junk inputs. The actual iff says the output is elliptic exactly when E is elliptic and D is a unit. The split parameters (1,0) return E identically; double twisting is isomorphic to E when D is a unit. In characteristic two the t=1,n=−d formulas retain the Artin–Schreier contribution a₂↦a₂+d a₁² and a₆↦a₆+d a₃². Thus the definition does not collapse all characteristic-two twists. Its given t,n are data, while changing a quadratic generator gives an explicit variable change, not equality of coefficient tuples.

The support condition is the zero-boundary normalization: a nonzero constant function cannot satisfy it on all of Euclidean space. Dimension n+1 supplies an actual coordinate. The derivative norm is the operator norm of the real Fréchet derivative, so bounding its application to a unit coordinate vector introduces no extra factor.

I inspected the one-dimensional FTC/Hölder proof, the measure-preserving coordinate chart, the Fubini argument for finite p and the separate essential-supremum argument for p=∞. Continuity of Du upgrades its almost-everywhere bound to every line, avoiding the invalid restriction of an arbitrary null set to a chosen line. The codomain need not be complete: the FTC argument passes through its completion. Infinite seminorms are permitted in ℝ≥0∞, without subtracting infinities or converting them to reals. Reversed and zero-width intervals force u=0; the 0·∞ convention consequently creates no spurious nonzero example. No sharp-constant claim is made.

I compared [Henkel's Theorem1.6 and its Baire step](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1407.5647), which treat continuous linear maps over rings with units tending to zero. The displayed theorem weakens the target assumptions to Baire and separates the scalar-action continuity used by the proof. Its source retains a complete first-countable nonarchimedean domain, so it does not purport to reproduce every general topological-module case of that paper.

I inspected both formal steps: the countable unit dilates cover the target by surjectivity and equivariance, giving interior of a closed image by Baire; then a decreasing open-subgroup basis and completeness give a convergent correction series, removing the closure. T0 of the target topological group supplies the separation needed to identify its two limits. Continuity of the additive map at zero gives global continuity, so no missing continuity hypothesis is concealed. For the scalars, invertibility makes each target action a homeomorphism; no scalar distributivity beyond the explicitly used equivariance is required. Thus a monoid-with-zero suffices for this general formulation.

The source need not be separated: convergence of its correction series suffices, and uniqueness is needed only after mapping into N. The trivial groups are harmless. A nontrivial discrete field cannot provide the hypothesized unit sequence tending to zero, preventing misuse of the theorem on arbitrary algebraic surjections. The choice of sequence or neighborhood basis does not enter the conclusion. The quotient-map corollary and the closed-range strictness application both pass with their stated hypotheses. The roadmap's discrete/adic/Tate-ring and Tate-algebra examples test the preceding ring constructions; no separate concrete Check is attached to this open-mapping step. Wedhorn was not independently read.

The [finite-divisor formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/LevelOne/FundamentalDomainBoundary/ValencePV.lean#L791) is the level-one valence identity with one representative from every ordinary boundary orbit. The three sums are over the strict interior, the left vertical boundary, and the left half of the unit arc with ρ removed. The elliptic point i has weight1/2, ρ has weight1/3, and the width-one q-expansion contributes its unnormalized integer order. The right boundary partners are deliberately omitted; counting both partners with full weight would double the divisor contribution.

The finite set S must capture every nonzero order in the closed fundamental domain and must contain no nonzero-order point outside it. Extra order-zero points do not affect the sum. These are real divisor-support hypotheses, not the desired identity in disguise. I inspected the canonical fdZeros construction and the subsequent valence_formula proof which supplies S and rewrites the result over all nonelliptic orbits, meeting [human roadmap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms/README.md#L327). The present finite-set statement therefore has the documented scope; it is not mislabeled as a sum over all points of ℍ.

Holomorphy and nonzero f on the connected upper half-plane rule out the junk-zero conventions of meromorphicOrderAt. Nonzero cusp expansion rules out the infinite-order-to-zero fallback there as well. Height and the nonvanishing punctured q-disk are constructed internally from the divisor bound and cusp analyticity, rather than assumed by the caller. Negative or odd weights admitting no nonzero level-one form cause no inconsistency; the hypotheses explicitly require such a form. The nonzero constant weight-zero case has all orders zero.

The boundary-calibration checks in the completed ContourIntegration roadmap have concrete witnesses here: the actual clockwise contour has winding−1/2 at smooth arc points, including i, and−1/6 at each of ρ and ρ+1. I read those value proofs and the half-residue specialization of the generalized residue theorem. The sign of the contour identity is reversed in the assembled valence proof, producing the positive weights displayed above. Thus the two corner contributions really sum to1/3; the values are not assumptions standing in for geometry. The source proof and full-orbit corollary pass inspection. Comparison uses the explicit human valence and contour specifications; Diamond–Shurman was not freshly read.

The [predicate](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/WeightedRestrictedSeries/Basic.lean#L413) is the coefficient condition in [Wedhorn, Definition5.48, equation5.6.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.05934), with finitely many variables as explicitly documented. For each open additive subgroup U, all but finitely many coefficients aν belong to Tν·U. The exceptional finite set may depend on U. Tν is the product of the set powers, and weightMul takes the additive subgroup generated by pointwise products, rather than incorrectly requiring that the raw product set itself be additive.

The weaker hypotheses of the bare predicate are deliberate. Multiplicative closure and the weighted ring topology require NonarchimedeanRing and the separately supplied IsWeightFamily; the definition does not assert them for arbitrary weights. In particular the [human roadmap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces/README.md#L200) standing openness condition has not been silently removed from the construction of the ring. Outside nonarchimedean topology this predicate need not mean ordinary coefficient convergence: the module documentation explicitly explains its vacuity over ℝ with trivial weights. The finite-variable restriction is also explicit, rather than a claim to have implemented Wedhorn's arbitrary index set.

I read the actual normalization proofs: for Tᵢ={1}, weightMul is U and restrictedness is equivalent to coefficient convergence when open subgroups form a basis. Finite-support series satisfy the condition for every weight. Over a discrete ring, the open zero subgroup forces finite support and recovers the polynomial ring. In zero variables the cofinite condition is vacuous for the correct reason: there is just the constant coefficient, and the proved comparison is evaluation at that coefficient. Empty weights force eventual vanishing in the affected positive degrees; they do not introduce division by zero. These tests calibrate the predicate without claiming completion or a universal property under its bare hypotheses. The roadmap has no additional concrete Check attached to this coefficient-definition clause.

The [degree formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Isogeny/Frobenius/Basic.lean#L149) computes the degree of the actual q-power Frobenius pullback, with q the cardinality of the finite base field. It uses q, rather than the characteristic p: q-powering fixes every base scalar and is therefore an F-algebra map. Over a nonprime finite field p-powering alone would not have that property. The pullback is extended from the coordinate ring to its fraction field by uniqueness, and the pointwise theorem identifies it on every rational function.

Degree is the dimension over the image subfield. I inspected the field tower: F(x^q) lies below both F(x) and F(W)^q, their relevant relative degrees are q and two, and transport by the injective Frobenius preserves the latter degree. The tower comparison gives [F(W):F(W)^q]=q. This is a field degree, not the number of geometric points of a purely inseparable kernel. The source separately proves separable degree one and inseparable degree q. Since F is a field and explicitly finite, q≥2, so Nat.card's infinite default and the zero/one exponents cannot enter.

Ellipticity is unnecessary for this function-field calculation: the affine Weierstrass equation supplies the quadratic extension of F(x) used in the tower. Singular models remain within this algebraic degree statement; the theorem does not declare them elliptic curves or identify their full group schemes. For elliptic W it gives precisely [human roadmap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves/README.md#L463) Layer1 and Silverman II.2.11(c) as specified there. Relative Frobenius over imperfect fields is a different, semilinear construction with a twisted target, not asserted here.

The inspected pullback, pure-inseparability and nonidentity witnesses pass and pin the intended map. There is no separately tagged numerical Check for this degree supplier; Hasse bounds and the degree of 1−Frobenius are later targets. A locally chosen Fintype only enumerates the finite field and does not alter the statement. Silverman's original text was not freshly read.

Separability and quadratic degree give a genuine nontrivial involution of L/K. The trace and norm therefore have their finite-extension meanings, not infinite-dimensional defaults. The [bounded real-integral formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/Contour/Winding/RealIntegral/OnCurve.lean#L482) concerns the generalized, potentially noninteger winding number, defined by the geometric Cauchy principal value of (z−s)⁻¹ divided by 2πi. I inspected the principal-value predicate: it removes a common Euclidean ε-ball around s, requires eventual integrability of the truncated integrands, and then takes ε→0⁺. It is not an unrelated principal value obtained by deleting equal parameter intervals at a corner.

The immersion hypothesis supplies nonzero one-sided tangents on finitely many C¹ pieces. The extra regularity is Lipschitz continuity of derivWithin on each side of every crossing; these tangents need not agree. Closedness plus γ(a)≠s puts all crossings in the interior. These are sufficient local conditions for the bounded-integrand part of [Hungerbühler–Wasem Proposition2.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1808.00997), whose statement and corner discussion I read. They do not assert a curvature value under only C¹,¹ regularity; that requires the separate C² result. This distinction matches the [human roadmap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/Completed/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/Completed/ContourIntegration/README.md#L145).

The real integrand is Im((γ−s)⁻¹γ′), with the coordinate numerator xẏ−yẋ and denominator x²+y². At a crossing its totalized value is zero, and the finite exceptional set does not change the integral. The source separately proves boundedness and ordinary interval integrability, and supplies a genuine complex principal-value witness. Thus neither the limUnder winding value nor a nonintegrable Bochner integral is being used in its fallback case. The real part of that witness is log|γ(b)−s|−log|γ(a)−s|, which vanishes by closedness. Reversed intervals carry the usual negative orientation; a=b gives zero.

The relevant [winding-number acceptance checks](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/Completed/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/Completed/ContourIntegration/README.md#L219) pass in proved source: the closed model sector has winding α/(2π), with smooth crossing α=π giving 1/2, and a counterclockwise circle has value1 inside and0 outside. I read their principal-value and circle-integral calculations. The simple-pole residue and improper-integral examples test later residue-theorem exports, not this real-integrand identity. No parametrization choice or preferred rounding to an integer enters the statement.

The [domain is the lattice of intermediate fields inside the relative separable closure](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/FieldTheory/Galois/AbsoluteGaloisGroup/Basic.lean#L229), not all intermediate fields of the normal ambient extension. The inverse takes a closed subgroup's fixed field in the ambient field and intersects it with that separable closure. The order dual correctly reverses inclusion. I checked both inverse equations and the restriction equivalence of topological Galois groups: injectivity uses pure inseparability of the remaining extension, surjectivity uses normality, and inverse continuity is proved using finite-subextension fixing neighbourhoods.

This intersection is essential over imperfect fields. For the purely inseparable extension `F_p(t^(1/p))/F_p(t)`, every base automorphism is trivial and the relative separable closure is just the base, so the two lattices in the theorem are singletons. Using all ambient intermediate fields would fail. Conversely, for a Galois ambient extension the separable closure is the whole extension and this recovers the ordinary infinite Galois correspondence. The bottom field corresponds to the whole group and the top separable field to the trivial subgroup. Closedness cannot be discarded, since taking a fixed field only detects a subgroup's closure.

These checks directly address the [ProfiniteCohomology imperfect-base warning](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology/README.md#L443), without confusing transport of the group with transport of its coefficient field or action. The separately proved fixing-subgroup intersection identity is the substantive guard. The purely inseparable example above is a mathematical specialization, not a new compiled fixture. This precisely realizes the [Polynomial Galois Groups layer 2 double-transitivity target](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/PolynomialGaloisGroups/README.md#L687). The divisor is the linear factor of the chosen actual root; no arbitrary algebraic element or chosen enumeration is substituted.

The key semantic point is [the equivariant identification](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/FieldTheory/GaloisGroups/MultipleTransitivity.lean#L40) of the point-stabilizer action on all other roots with the roots of the quotient over `F(x)`. Thus the usual transitive-root/irreducible-polynomial criterion applies to the relative Galois group, exactly the stabilizer argument behind the cited permutation-theoretic criterion.

The degree hypothesis is essential for the intended convention: for a linear polynomial there are no ordered pairs of distinct roots, while the quotient is a nonzero constant and hence not irreducible. Degree two is correctly included: the remaining factor is linear. Monicity of the original polynomial is unnecessary since the divisor is monic and multiplication by a nonzero scalar does not change irreducibility. These edge assessments are mathematical, not claims of separately run examples.

The reference measure fixes a nontrivial constant. [symmetricLebesgue](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Measure/SymmetricMatrix/Lebesgue.lean#L54) is product Lebesgue measure in the independent upper-triangular entries. Frobenius volume is larger by 2^(p(p−1)/4), as the proved comparison records. Thus replacing the displayed measure by generic Euclidean volume would change the answer. The symmetric carrier retains its subtype topology and uniformity; the Frobenius instances rebuild the metric compatibly rather than introducing a new topology.

The Cholesky proof yields diagonal factors 2t^(2a−i−1)exp(−t²) on t>0 and unrestricted off-diagonal Gaussians. The bound a>(p−1)/2 makes every Gamma argument a−i/2 positive. There are p(p−1)/2 off-diagonal coordinates, giving π^(p(p−1)/4); all exponents in Γ_p use real casts, so no natural-number division truncates them. Positive diagonal entries make the Gram parametrization injective and the Jacobian nonnegative. No value of a chosen Cholesky factor outside the positive-definite cone is used.

The Bochner integral is not silently the default zero for a nonintegrable function: integrability and the finite lower-integral value are separately proved. At p=0 the cone is one point, its measure is Dirac, and the separate theorem gives 1 for every a; the present theorem merely carries an unnecessary restriction in that dimension. At p=1 the measure-preserving scalar coordinate and Γ₁=Γ recover Euler's integral for a>0.

The outward sign is verified by the last analytic step, not inferred from the word maximum. Along x₀−he with h>0 the perturbed function stays below u(x₀). Its right derivative gives D_eu(x₀)≥ε(−p)R^(p−1)>0. Here the [barrier](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Laplacian/HopfLemma.lean#L86) is ‖x−y‖^p−R^p with p<0, and is used only on the annulus R/2≤‖x−y‖≤R, so its singular value at y never enters a differentiability claim.

Compactness and continuity provide a uniform positive gap on the inner sphere. A sufficiently small positive multiple of the barrier preserves the boundary upper bound; its computed Laplacian and the weak maximum principle extend that bound over the annulus. In the pure-Laplacian specialization, subtracting u(x₀) removes the general zeroth-order theorem's boundary nonnegativity assumption. The current corollary then derives the strict interior and weak sphere bounds from its stronger closed-ball maximum hypothesis.

The explicit DifferentiableAt assumption excludes a default-zero fderiv at the boundary. Only interior C² regularity is required. R>0 and ‖e‖=1 exclude an empty sphere and the zero-dimensional case; finite dimensionality supplies compact balls. A linear height function u(x)=⟪x−y,e⟫ has Δu=0, unique closed-ball maximum at y+Re, and outward derivative 1, confirming the sign and nonvacuity by direct mathematical calculation. Constant functions fail the strict maximum assumption.

The additional checks concern the level and scalar normalization. [The theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/NumberTheory/HeckeRing/GL2/Gamma0/Diagonal/Composite.lean#L305) is in the actual integral double-coset Hecke ring; `T_n` is assembled from the prime-power recurrence family. Its [prime and prime-power comparisons](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/NumberTheory/HeckeRing/GL2/Gamma0/Diagonal/Composite.lean#L156) fix the initial generator to `diag(1,p)`. The scalar is the guarded double coset `diag(d,d)`, and [it vanishes when d shares a factor with N](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/NumberTheory/HeckeRing/GL2/Gamma0/Diagonal/PrimePower.lean#L140). Consequently summing over all gcd divisors agrees with restricting to divisors prime to the level. This is why no coprimality of m or n with N is required.

The coefficient is integer multiplication by d in the ring. After acting on weight-k forms, the [proved coefficient formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/HeckeSlash/Nebentypus/CoefficientFormula.lean#L86) becomes `χ(d)d^(k−1)`, confirming the classical normalization rather than assuming an operator convention. Both m,n must be nonzero: the documented `T_0=1` and empty divisors of zero make the omitted (0,0) instance false. For gcd1 the sum reduces to coprime multiplicativity; bad-prime powers reduce to powers of `T_p`.

Exact-name search finds ModularForms PROGRESS and [Layer 2's ring/action contracts](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms/README.md#L393). The coprime and bad-prime regressions and action calibration pass by complete source proofs without `sorry`; no separate tagged divisor-table Check is listed. Shimura 3.24(3) and Diamond–Shurman §5.3 are the source locators; full-book consultation and a successful local rebuild are not claimed.

The universal-base argument justifies the apparent generality in the rendered statement. [formalAdd](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/FormalGroup/Add/Series.lean#L84) is the inverse of the chord's third-intersection parameter, so it is the curve's addition series. In [associativity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/FormalGroup/Add/Assoc.lean#L672), the three distinct variables are exactly the left, middle and right summands; nested substitutions give the two bracketings, without permuting inputs. The zero constant coefficient makes these substitutions legitimate.

The proof first identifies both expressions with the same sum of three points over the universal fraction field, and then transports the identity through specialization. [Base-change compatibility](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/FormalGroup/Add/Series.lean#L115) is proved, not an unverified assumption. This permits arbitrary commutative coefficient rings, including nilpotents and characteristics two or three: no division by 2, 3 or the discriminant is imposed on the target ring. A singular special fibre does not invalidate the formal identity at the smooth point at infinity.

The rendered conclusion suppresses the type of the last existential witness. [The source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Analysis/Complex/Conformal/Jordan/Approach.lean#L214) makes it a homeomorphism from the actual closed unit disc to `closure Ω`, and explicitly identifies its values with the same holomorphic function g that maps the open disc bijectively onto Ω. Hence the theorem gives a conformal extension, not an unrelated topological homeomorphism of two closures.

`IsJordanCurve (frontier Ω)` means [the frontier is homeomorphic to the circle](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Topology/JordanCurve/Basic.lean#L109); it does not already package the sought disc extension. Openness, connectedness and boundedness select the bounded Jordan domain and exclude an exterior region; `IsConnected` also includes nonemptiness. No smoothness, rectifiability or analyticity of the boundary is silently required. Injective holomorphy on the disc supplies conformality there; boundary points need only continuity. Existence makes normalization and automorphism choices harmless.

[ConformalMapping L5](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/ConformalMapping/README.md#L124) asks precisely for this Jordan-domain closure theorem, excluding the separate prime-end generalization. L5 lists no additional tagged Check. The indexing and the analytic convergence are the useful additional checks. In [the source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/NumberTheory/ArithmeticDirichletSeries/EulerProduct/Analytic.lean#L498), the product runs over `HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K)`, so it counts each nonzero prime ideal separately even when several primes have equal norm. The norm is the absolute ideal norm; no rational-prime regrouping or residue-degree factor is silently substituted. The expression uses ordinary complex powers of positive integer norms, and `Re s>1` makes each geometric ratio have norm below one.

The proof obtains absolute summability of the trivial ideal-weight series on that half-plane, applies the general unrestricted `HasProd` theorem, and uses the explicit identification with `NumberField.dedekindZeta`. Thus it is stronger than an ordered or formal Euler product. The multiplicative weight's zero-ideal value is zero, so no undefined norm-zero term is introduced. No assertion is made at the pole or in the analytic-continuation region.

The omitted complex alternative is justified by the centrality hypothesis, not by treating ℂ as an invalid real algebra. In the pinned [negative-control proof](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Algebra/CentralSimple/BaseChange.lean#L199), an assumed `IsCentral ℝ ℂ` forces the central element i into the real scalar image; imaginary parts then give a contradiction. This supplies an actual source regression for the roadmap's centrality obstruction, albeit inside an anonymous base-change example rather than a standalone named lemma.

The [classification](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Algebra/CentralSimple/Real.lean#L374) uses positive degree and its bound by two, with degree squared equal to real dimension. The degree-one branch constructs the scalar algebra equivalence. The [four-dimensional branch](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Algebra/CentralSimple/Real.lean#L331) constructs two anticommuting elements with squares −1, obtains the Hamilton-quaternion algebra homomorphism, and proves it bijective by injectivity and equal dimensions. Thus the result is an ℝ-algebra equivalence, not merely an equality of dimensions or an abstract ring isomorphism. Division-ring nontriviality excludes the zero ring; higher matrix algebras do not satisfy the division hypothesis.

[SemisimpleAlgebras Layer 6](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/SemisimpleAlgebras/README.md#L318) is the exact target. Tensor-square splitting and Brauer-group generation are further targets, not additional conclusions here. This agrees with the central noncommutative classification in [Conrad, Theorem 7.4](https://ctnt-summer-math.media.uconn.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/1632/2024/06/CTNT-usingQR.pdf). It internally completes the square by an admissible variable change and transports finite generation through the actual additive equivalence of point groups. `W.Point` includes the point at infinity, so this is the full elliptic-curve group, not the affine solutions with the identity omitted.

The arithmetic hypotheses are discharged for every irreducible factor field of the transformed cubic: [class-group finiteness and unit finite generation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/MordellWeil/FinitelyGenerated.lean#L125) concern the integral closures in those fields, not only the original ring of integers. Ellipticity supplies the nonsingular curve required by the height and weak-descent arguments; singular cubics and arbitrary characteristic-zero fields are not included. The conclusion gives finite generation, not generators, a rank formula or an algorithm for rational points.

I compared the statement and variable-change step with [Stoll's cited pinned implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MichaelStollBayreuth/EllipticCurves/66889eada51a74c2f5dfb7fb5909b0b5a0a2d96e/EllipticCurves/MordellWeil.lean), which states the same generality. Under the explicit finite-generation assumption this torsion-free integer module admits a finite basis, and the chosen `Module.finBasis` enters only through the Gram determinant of the descended Néron–Tate pairing.

The choice check is stronger than permutation invariance: an arbitrary change of **integral basis** transforms the matrix by congruence, and its unimodular determinant has square one. The inspected API also handles different basis index types by reindexing before comparing determinants. The pairing is its halved polarization and has that height on the diagonal. Consequently rescaling to the other height convention would divide the rank-r regulator by `2^r`; the definition consistently retains the pinned convention. Rank zero uses the empty determinant and returns one, even though the quotient has only its zero point.

The parameter being uniquely determined is the subgroup `H`, while the comparison homeomorphism is existential. Its two compatibility conditions require both preservation of the chosen lift and commutation with projection to `X`; omitting the first would leave only a conjugacy class, not a unique subgroup.

The witness is the actual image of the induced fundamental-group map of `p`, with the basepoint equality transported by `mapOfEq`. The subgroup quotient is the orbit quotient of the based-path universal cover by `H`, not an abstract set of cosets assigned a convenient topology. Local path-connectedness is obtained for the total spaces from the covering maps before applying the pointed comparison theorem.

The [recovered-subgroup calculation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/UniversalCover/Classification/RecoveredSubgroup.lean#L176) checks the left-action convention: the quotient's fundamental group identifies with the opposite group of `H`, and the endpoint map uses an inverse. Taking its range nevertheless gives exactly `H`, since a subgroup is closed under inverses. This prevents an unnoticed opposite/conjugate subgroup from entering the uniqueness proof.

The target deliberately omits global path-connectedness of `X`. Its pointed path-connected total space lies over the component of `x₀`; the quotient projection has exactly that component as its range, with empty fibres elsewhere. It does not claim a surjective connected cover of a disconnected base. At the subgroup extremes, the trivial quotient is the universal cover and the whole-group quotient has injective endpoint projection.

These checks address the [roadmap's pointed/unpointed distinction and convention requirement](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/Completed/UniversalCovers/README.md#L89). The [pinned proof](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Combinatorics/DenseGraphLimits/Applications.lean#L433) establishes t(C₄,W)≥t(K₂,W)⁴ for a symmetric measurable [0,1]-valued graphon on an arbitrary probability space. These are homomorphism densities, with one factor per unordered edge, rather than injective or induced densities. I checked the explicit four-edge integral and its conversion to ∫B(x,z)², where B(x,z)=∫W(x,y)W(y,z)dy. Symmetry supplies the repeated two-step factor; boundedness and the probability hypothesis supply integrability and the unit normalization.

The two Cauchy–Schwarz steps give ∫B²≥(∫B)²=(∫degree²)²≥(∫degree)⁴. All quantities squared are nonnegative; no division by a possibly zero edge density occurs. For constant W=p this is equality p⁴≥p⁴, including p=0 and p=1. Atomic carriers are allowed, with no concealed atomlessness or standard-Borel premise.

For the [roadmap's acceptance gates](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/DenseGraphLimits/README.md#L656), the actual constant-density theorem and the computed values t(K₂,W_K₄)=3/4, t(K₃,W_C₅)=0, and t(K₃,W_1/2)=1/8 calibrate both edge counting and normalization. The finite-graph comparison explicitly requires a nonempty host, avoiding 0/0. [Cut-distance-zero invariance](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Combinatorics/DenseGraphLimits/Separation/Forward.lean#L62) and `homDensityOnSpace_mk` show that both sides descend to graphon space, so the raw-carrier statement has the required quotient meaning. Correctly stated as Dirichlet-density Chebotarev. I read the [rendered theorem and reduction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/NumberTheory/Chebotarev/Density/Chebotarev.lean#L53) and [Sharifi Theorem 7.2.2](https://www.math.ucla.edu/~sharifi/notes/algnum-ch07.html). The finite Galois group and every conjugacy-class carrier are nonempty; therefore #C/#G is positive with a nonzero denominator. The trivial extension gives all primes and density1. No representative is chosen in the public result.

The [prime set](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/NumberTheory/Chebotarev/FrobeniusPrimeSet.lean#L89) consists of actual height-one primes of the ring of integers of K, with unramifiedness required before constructing the Artin class. HasDirichletDensity is the genuine limit, as s→1⁺, of the prime sum divided by the all-prime sum; it is not a totalized density value. These settle [acceptance checks1,3,5](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/Chebotarev/README.md#L634), including ramification junk.

Its domain structure is derived from injectivity into `L`, so an arbitrary abstract representative `C` is legitimate. The fraction-field comparison then makes the integral-closedness argument meaningful: an element integral over `C` is integral over `A` and hence belongs to `C`. Neither normality of `A` nor separability of `L/K` has slipped into the hypotheses. This agrees with [Stacks 09IG](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09IG).

The zero-dimensional boundary is intentional: Mathlib's Dedekind convention includes fields. Taking `A=K` and any finite field extension `L` gives `C≃L`; a singular one-dimensional domain is also allowed, since normality is required of its normalization rather than its source. Domain and finite-extension assumptions exclude zero-ring or infinite-algebraic-extension substitutes. All scalar towers identify the stated structure maps, and no arbitrary model choice appears in the conclusion.

For the [AlgebraicCurves Layer 2 requirement](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicCurves/README.md#L436), I explicitly separated this theorem from module finiteness. Krull–Akizuki alone does not prove that stronger milestone. The independently defined [polynomial normalization theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/RingTheory/IntegralClosure/MvPolynomial.lean#L92) supplies finiteness even without separability, through the Japanese/purely-inseparable development; its transcendental-adjoin transport is also present. Thus accepting this Dedekind bridge does not silently replace the roadmap's stronger normalization requirement. This adds the model, inseparability, and finiteness checks to the prior descriptive record. Source and extractor evidence were inspected; no local Lean compilation is claimed.

It does not claim finite generation over the original ring. I traced the [abstract proof and length bound](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/RingTheory/IntegralClosure/NormalizationFinite.lean#L265): the zero ideal is handled separately; every nonzero ideal contracts to a nonzero element `a` of `A`; the bound for `C/aC` gives finite length over `A`; lifting generators then gives finite generation as a `C`-ideal. This is the substantive mechanism of [Stacks' Krull–Akizuki lemma](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00PG), rather than a circular appeal to Noetherianity of `C`.

The ambient `L` need only be a domain with a compatible `K`-module structure: the proof uses its vector-space dimension and the injective algebra map from `C`, not field operations in `L`. The scalar-tower assumptions make multiplication by `a` the same operation in the quotient and the ambient module. The nonzero restriction on `a` prevents the length bound from asserting finiteness of `C` itself. Fields, integral closures already equal to `A`, and inseparable finite extensions are legitimate boundaries; dimension greater than one and infinite-dimensional ambient spaces are excluded.

The kernel is proved to be all rational points using the [tautological-point/pullback calculation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Isogeny/OneSubFrobenius/Kernel.lean#L65). For the other inequality, an embedding of the pulled-back function field gives the rational point by which it moves the generic point; [injectivity of this assignment](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Isogeny/OneSubFrobenius/Degree.lean#L66) bounds the number of embeddings. The displayed current definition agrees with the [pinned source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/RingTheory/Valuation/Microbial.lean#L88) and [Wedhorn5.46(v)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.05934v1), which I read: the valuation's value group must admit a height-one ordered quotient. The convex subgroup is taken in the units of v.ValueGroup₀, the group generated by nonzero values, rather than in an arbitrary ambient codomain. Enlarging the target of a trivial valuation therefore cannot falsely make it microbial.

The two quotient conditions are both necessary. [MulArchimedean](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Algebra/Order/Group/ConvexSubgroup.lean#L562) is equivalent to having only bottom and top convex subgroups; adding Nontrivial excludes the height-zero quotient. In particular H=⊤ cannot supply a witness. H=⊥ does supply one when the actual value group is nontrivial and archimedean. The general ring-valued signature extends Wedhorn's field formulation by this intrinsic group condition; it does not assert all his field-topological equivalences for arbitrary rings.

Accept as the displayed law-invariance predicate. The [definition](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/Probability/Exchangeability/Arrays/Basic.lean#L110) quantifies over two independent permutations of ℕ acting on the two coordinates of the full array path space. It neither permutes entries arbitrarily nor restricts both axes to the same permutation. Consequently it is stronger than joint exchangeability but weaker than exchangeability of the entire ℕ×ℕ-indexed family. I checked the actual counterexample: the deterministic diagonal-indicator array is jointly invariant, while swapping rows 0 and 1 changes the (0,0) entry and hence its Dirac path law under a probability measure.

The definition itself intentionally packages only equality of pushforward measures. It does not assert that X is measurable or μ is a probability measure; those hypotheses must accompany probabilistic uses, since Lean's total `Measure.map` is not a probability-law certificate for a non-a.e.-measurable map. The module states that limitation, and `map_comp`, row exchangeability and the de Finetti consumers supply coordinate a.e. measurability. The zero measure therefore gives a harmless law-level degenerate case, not a claim about random arrays under a probability law.

The [Exchangeability roadmap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/TauCetiRoadmap/Exchangeability/README.md#L994) names arrays as a later extension, without imposing the entire Aldous–Hoover representation on this foundational predicate. The actual i.i.d.-array introduction theorem and diagonal positive/negative controls give nonvacuous witnesses for the intended distinction. Infinite permutations are compatible with full path-law invariance on the countable product. Source, rendered definition and prior records were inspected; no local Lean compilation is claimed.

I unfolded [HasAnalyticExtensionAt](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/715f34bfe19bf093e063fd400854602b1effc927/TauCeti/NumberTheory/LSeries/Landau.lean#L137): a positive-radius complex disc carries a holomorphic function agreeing with the Dirichlet series on its intersection with Re(s)>σ. The strict half-plane lies inside actual convergence because the hypothesis identifies σ with the finite absolute abscissa; therefore equality with totalized `LSeries` does not merely identify two junk zeros. Nonnegativity in `ComplexOrder` means real nonnegative coefficients, not just nonnegative real parts.

The proof patches the continuation with the convergent series, expands at σ+1, and uses alternating derivatives so that evaluating the Taylor series to the left yields nonnegative summands. The summability comparison then forces convergence at x<σ, contradicting the exact abscissa. This is a local singularity statement, not an unsupported assertion of a pole; the separate meromorphic-order corollary adds meromorphic continuation. Finite-support and zero coefficients have abscissa −∞ and are excluded by the real-equality hypothesis. The ignored coefficient at index zero is an unnecessary restriction in this version, removed by the adjacent ordinary-abscissa variant.

The [ArithmeticDirichletSeries Layer-8 contract](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/eafdde47e47e067afa9c64faddc70703a69c7c56/Completed/ArithmeticDirichletSeries/README.md#L320) explicitly requires the actual finite boundary, the nonnegative ordinary/absolute comparison, and the meromorphic corollary; all are present. The positive control proves analytic continuation strictly inside the convergence half-plane, so the extension predicate is not vacuously impossible.
